info.name: semantic-router
info.description:
vLLM Semantic Router (ai/semantic-router/). Two ways in, and they authenticate DIFFERENTLY:

1. Direct at Envoy on {{semanticRouter}} (host publish PORT_SEMANTIC_ROUTER, default http://localhost:8025, container port 8899). Bearer token is {{listener key}} = SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LISTENER_KEY, checked by a Lua filter in the generated Envoy config. The folder 'Envoy listener (direct)' overrides the collection auth with it. This is the debugging path.

2. Through LiteLLM on {{litellm}} as the model `auto`. Bearer token is {{virtual master key}}, a normal LiteLLM virtual key -- LiteLLM attaches the listener key itself. This is what Open WebUI and every other client actually does.

TWO LAYERS. The router only picks a CHAIN: four `static` decisions, each forwarding the request (one call, no fan-out) to one LiteLLM chain alias -- privacy_local -> local-private, code -> local-code, reasoning -> local-reasoning, everything else -> local-general. LiteLLM then picks the backend by `order`: local models first (qwen3.8-solo / muse-glimmer), Claude only when BOTH are busy or down (ai/litellm/overflow.py), and never for local-private. The router swaps the Authorization header for SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LITELLM_KEY on the forwarded request, so spend lands on the router's key.

NO OTHER ROUTER PORT IS PUBLISHED. The router's ext_proc gRPC (50051), management API (8080) and metrics (9190), and Envoy's admin (9901), are reachable only from inside the container network. There is no collection item for them on purpose -- if you need one, `docker exec` into a container on ai_shared.

WHY THERE IS ONLY ONE ROUTER ENTRYPOINT: vllm-sr 0.3.0 has no `entrypoints:` block and no per-algorithm model names. Exactly one name, global.router.auto_model_name (`vllm-sr/auto`), triggers routing; which chain is used is chosen by which DECISION the request's signals match. The items below exercise each decision by sending a prompt shaped to trip its signal. The release's looper algorithms (confidence / ratings / remom) are NOT used -- they were removed for cost; Fusion and Workflows do not exist in 0.3.0 at all.

See ai/semantic-router/SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md for the two layers, the decisions table, the privacy guarantee, and the verification checklist; ai/litellm/LITELLM.md > Chain aliases and the overflow hook for layer 2.

variable.description: Envoy listener base URL. Host publish is PORT_SEMANTIC_ROUTER (8025 by default) mapped to container port 8899; on ai_shared it is http://vllm-sr-envoy:8899. Not fronted by oauth2-proxy -- the listener bearer token is the only thing in front of it, so do not expose 8025 on an untrusted network.

SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LISTENER_KEY from .env. Used ONLY by the 'Envoy listener (direct)' folder, which overrides the collection auth with it. Anyone holding it can spend model tokens through the whole candidate pool, Anthropic included -- treat it like a production password. Rotating it is: edit .env, `make up semantic-router` (a recreate, so vllm-sr-models-init re-substitutes it into the Envoy config), then `make up litellm`.
LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it is http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it is https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI -> Virtual Keys, or /key/generate). Must be scoped to allow the `auto` alias. This is NOT SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LITELLM_KEY -- that one belongs to the router and is deliberately scoped to the four chain aliases (local-general, local-code, local-reasoning, local-private) and nothing else, so using it here would 401 on `auto`. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

item.name: Envoy listener (direct)
item.description: Straight at the router's Envoy listener on {{semanticRouter}}, bypassing LiteLLM. Overrides the collection bearer with {{listener key}}. Use these to decide whether a problem is in the router or in the LiteLLM leg in front of it.

request.description:
Lists what the router will accept as a `model` value: the auto entrypoint (`vllm-sr/auto`, from global.router.auto_model_name) plus the four chain aliases (local-general, local-code, local-reasoning, local-private), because global.router.include_config_models_in_list is true in config.yaml.

Returns the OpenAI /v1/models shape. 401 with `{"error":{"code":"invalid_api_key"}}` if the bearer token is missing or wrong -- that 401 comes from the Envoy Lua filter, not from the router, so seeing it means Envoy is up and the listener key is the problem. Connection refused means vllm-sr-envoy is not running or PORT_SEMANTIC_ROUTER is not published.

See SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Ports and exposure.

The catch-all decision `general` (priority 10, `conditions: []`). Nothing in this prompt trips the privacy, code or reasoning keyword signals, so the router forwards it -- one call, `static` -- to the LiteLLM chain `local-general`: qwen3.8-solo (order 1), then muse-glimmer (order 2), then claude-sonnet-5 (order 3) ONLY when both local models are busy (vLLM waiting queue for OVERFLOW_BUSY_AFTER_S) or down. With the box idle the spend log must show openai/qwen3.8-solo and no Claude row.

Returns a normal OpenAI chat completion. Which decision matched is in the router log (`make logs semantic-router vllm-sr-router`) and in the response's `route_diagnostics`; WHICH BACKEND ANSWERED is only in LiteLLM's spend log (Admin UI -> Logs, filter on the router's virtual key): model group = the chain alias, model = the deployment (openai/qwen3.8-solo, openai/muse-glimmer, anthropic/claude-*). SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Seeing what happened to a turn.

Errors: 401 from Envoy (listener key wrong / init substitution did not run); 401 from LiteLLM (SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LITELLM_KEY is not scoped to the chain alias the router picked -- it must list local-general, local-code, local-reasoning, local-private); 504 / empty body past 1800s (the chain never answered -- check LiteLLM and the vLLM queues).

SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Decisions.

Trips the `privacy_kw` signal (priority 300, matched before everything else), so the router forwards the request to the LiteLLM chain `local-private`: qwen3.8-solo, then muse-glimmer, and NOTHING ELSE. local-private has no Claude deployment and no entry in `fallbacks` / `context_window_fallbacks`: with both local models busy it queues locally (expect a slow answer, not a cloud one), with both down it fails.

This is the one item worth verifying in the LiteLLM Admin UI as well as here: after running it, the spend log must show model group local-private with a LOCAL model (openai/qwen3.8-solo or openai/muse-glimmer) -- a Claude model under local-private must never appear. If the row's model group is local-general instead, the keyword signal missed: add the term to `privacy_kw` in config.yaml.

Which decision matched is in the router log (`make logs semantic-router vllm-sr-router`) and in the response's `route_diagnostics`; WHICH BACKEND ANSWERED is only in LiteLLM's spend log (Admin UI -> Logs, filter on the router's virtual key): model group = the chain alias, model = the deployment (openai/qwen3.8-solo, openai/muse-glimmer, anthropic/claude-*). SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Seeing what happened to a turn.

SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > The privacy guarantee.

Trips `code_kw` (priority 200): decision `code`, forwarded -- one call, `static` -- to the LiteLLM chain `local-code`: qwen3.8-solo, then muse-glimmer, then claude-sonnet-5 only when both local models are busy or down. Same ladder as local-general, kept as its own group so code traffic can be re-tuned and attributed separately.

Expect no output until the chain has answered: Envoy runs ext_proc with buffered request and response bodies.

Which decision matched is in the router log (`make logs semantic-router vllm-sr-router`) and in the response's `route_diagnostics`; WHICH BACKEND ANSWERED is only in LiteLLM's spend log (Admin UI -> Logs, filter on the router's virtual key): model group = the chain alias, model = the deployment (openai/qwen3.8-solo, openai/muse-glimmer, anthropic/claude-*). SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Seeing what happened to a turn.

SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Decisions and > Concurrency budget.

Trips `reasoning_kw` (priority 150): decision `reasoning`, forwarded -- one call, `static` -- to the LiteLLM chain `local-reasoning`: muse-glimmer first (the reasoner), then qwen3.8-solo, then claude-opus-5-5 only when both local models are busy or down. (This used to be a 6-call remom loop; it was removed for cost.)

muse-glimmer's 4 vLLM sequences are shared with the classifier, so during a classifier batch the overflow hook may mark it busy and this lands on qwen3.8-solo -- check the spend log's model column.

Which decision matched is in the router log (`make logs semantic-router vllm-sr-router`) and in the response's `route_diagnostics`; WHICH BACKEND ANSWERED is only in LiteLLM's spend log (Admin UI -> Logs, filter on the router's virtual key): model group = the chain alias, model = the deployment (openai/qwen3.8-solo, openai/muse-glimmer, anthropic/claude-*). SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Seeing what happened to a turn.

SEMANTIC_ROUTER.md > Decisions and > Concurrency budget.

Sends a CONCRETE chain alias instead of the auto entrypoint. Only `vllm-sr/auto` triggers routing; anything else is treated as an explicit selection, and Envoy matches the x-selected-model header the router sets to that chain's cluster -- which, for every entry in the pool, is litellm:4000.

Use it to bisect: if this works and the `vllm-sr/auto` items do not, the Envoy -> LiteLLM leg is fine and the problem is in the decisions. If this fails too, the router cannot reach LiteLLM -- check SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LITELLM_KEY and its alias scoping.

Valid names here are exactly the providers.models entries in config.yaml: local-general, local-code, local-reasoning, local-private -- the four aliases SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LITELLM_KEY is scoped to. A concrete backend alias (qwen3.8-solo, claude-sonnet-5, ...) is NOT in the pool any more; an unknown name falls through to Envoy's default route, models[0] (local-general). This body uses local-private, so it can never reach Claude.

item.name: Through LiteLLM
item.description: The production path: model `auto` on {{litellm}}, authenticated with {{virtual master key}} via the collection-level auth. LiteLLM attaches the listener key server-side, so a chat client never sees it.

request.description:
The router alias should appear as `auto`. If it does not, LiteLLM has not reloaded ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`make up litellm`), or the virtual key in use is not scoped to it.

Uses the collection-level bearer, i.e. {{virtual master key}} -- NOT the listener key.

The real production path: Open WebUI and every other client call `auto` here, LiteLLM rewrites it to `vllm-sr/auto` and forwards to http://vllm-sr-envoy:8899/v1 with SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LISTENER_KEY attached server-side. The router picks a chain alias and the request comes back into LiteLLM under SEMANTIC_ROUTER_LITELLM_KEY. The caller never holds either key.

Compare the result with the equivalent item in the 'Envoy listener (direct)' folder: identical output means the LiteLLM leg is transparent; a difference means LiteLLM is transforming the body (check drop_params and the alias's max_tokens).

Errors worth knowing: `auto` declares max_input_tokens 245760 (muse-glimmer's window, the largest any path can serve locally); a longer prompt is refused, and `context_window_fallbacks: auto -> [local-private]` refuses it too -- it never reaches Claude. If vllm-sr-envoy is unreachable, `fallbacks: auto -> [local-private]` answers locally instead. Both are in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml.

Backend footer: the answer ends with `\n\n---\n*qwen3.8-solo · local-general*` -- the deployment and chain that actually served it, plus ` · overflow (local busy)` / `(local down)` when a Claude deployment answered and ` · router bypassed` on the fallback path. LiteLLM adds it to `auto` responses only (ai/litellm/overflow.py), so the 'Envoy listener (direct)' items never carry it -- the one expected difference between the two folders. It must agree with the `llm_provider-x-litellm-model-name` / `llm_provider-x-litellm-model-group` response headers. Footers in earlier assistant messages are stripped before the router sees the request; tool calls and `response_format` requests get none. AUTO_FOOTER_ENABLED=false turns it off. LITELLM.md > The `auto` footer.

Same path with stream: true. Worth running because the answer is NOT incremental in the way the caller expects: Envoy buffers the whole ext_proc request and response body, so the stream stays silent until the chain has answered and then delivers. Open WebUI shows a waiting state throughout.

This prompt trips `code_kw`, so it lands on the local-code chain -- one call to qwen3.8-solo (or muse-glimmer / claude-sonnet-5 if the overflow hook spilled).

If the stream dies early, the culprit is a stream_timeout below 1800 on the `auto` alias, or a listener timeout below 1800s in config.yaml. The two must stay in step.

The backend footer (`---` + `*<model> · <chain>*`) arrives as the last `delta.content`, just before the finish chunk and `data: [DONE]`. LITELLM.md > The `auto` footer.

Verification item, not an everyday call. Run `make down semantic-router vllm-sr-envoy`, then send this: LiteLLM should serve `auto` from the local-private chain via `fallbacks: auto -> [local-private]` -- qwen3.8-solo or muse-glimmer, NEVER Claude, because with the router down nothing has checked the prompt for PII. The spend log should show model group local-private under YOUR key with a local model.

A hard 5xx instead means the `auto` entry is missing from the `fallbacks` map in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml -- LiteLLM reports that as 'Available Model Group Fallbacks=None' -- or both local models are down too (local-private fails closed by design). Bring Envoy back with `make up semantic-router` afterwards.

The answer's footer should read `*qwen3.8-solo · local-private · router bypassed*` (or muse-glimmer). No `router bypassed` means the router answered after all. LITELLM.md > The `auto` footer.
